comments.text: Holding back the Arabian Gulf's currents on artificially dredged sand is a terrifyingly ambitious battle against nature. The sheer heat and saltwater erosion in that climate make long-term coastal preservation a constant effort. That contrast between scorching desert dust and reclaimed blue water is intense!

comments.text: Building massive residential islands out of sand and rock in the middle of the Gulf completely redefines human engineering, but maintaining them is an endless battle. Watching how they constantly fight erosion, rising sea levels, and extreme desert heat just to keep these islands from sinking is deeply humbling. It really shows that conquering the sea isn't a one-time achievement—it's a heavy, daily commitment to maintenance.
